newsitem.title: USA: CME to launch OSB lumber contract trading on Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: CME to launch OSB lumber contract trading on Nov 8.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said it will launch trading in its new Oriented Strand Board (OSB) futures contract on Friday, November 8.
The CME said OSB was an "environmentally friendly" panel material "quickly replacing plywood in the building of new homes, with sales of around $3 billion a year.
OSB futures will be traded in the same pit as the CME's Random Lengths 2x4 inch lumber contract, which was established in 1969.

OSB contract specifications call for delivery of 100,000 square feet of 4-foot by 8-foot panels, with prices quoted in U.S. dollars per 1,000 square feet. Contract months will be January, March, May, July, September and November.

OSB is an engineered wood product made of Aspen and other "weed" trees which regenerate when cut at the roots. Such trees contain abundant fiber but were considered too small to produce traditional solid building materials.

The trees are manufactured into wood strands and sawdust and bark residues used at plant sites to power furnaces. Added to the trees own regenerative properties, this contributes to OSB's claim to be environmentally friendly, the CME said.
Trade in OSB futures options will start on Monday, Nov 11.
